ledger.claim: The reroute was not traffic-justified, so the driver cannot reach the traffic-justified rows of POL-RD-24 at all. POL-RD-23 allows a reroute to be called traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The only such data in this record is the LTA advisory for Bedok Road - the recommended road - and its type is NONE, which is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names, even though the advisory covers the trip window (valid 10:58 to 12:28) and the exact segment (New Upper Changi Road to Upper East Coast Road) and reports 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded ... Speed bands 4-6 throughout'. The driver's statement that 'Bedok Road got bus stop and traffic light very long' is an assertion of traffic, and POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute.

The driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, so this was not an agreed deviation under POL-RD-21. That clause requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence. The chat log carries exactly two entries, both sent at 11:26 - before the 11:28:02 departure - and both about the pickup point, not the route; the trip record's own messages_during_trip is empty and its in_app_calls is empty; and the platform detected the deviation at 11:30:14 and the rejoin at 11:35:16. There is no in-app notice during the trip and no recorded verbal notice, so the driver cannot establish that the deviation was agreed, and no row of POL-RD-24 that depends on the rider's agreement is open to the driver.

The rider's account of the route is corroborated by the platform's own telemetry and by the trace. The trip record logs route_deviation_detected at 11:30:14 - the vehicle took Jalan Bilal where the recommended route is Bedok Road - and route_rejoined at 11:35:16, so the vehicle was off the recommended route for about five minutes; the driver-device trace's road sequence runs New Upper Changi Road, Jalan Bilal, Siglap Road, Upper East Coast Road, Marine Parade Road, which is the Siglap side-road route the rider complains of. The trace is used here only to show which route was taken and when, exactly as POL-RD-22 permits; it is not used to re-measure the distance.

The rider is straight with the judge about the distance, because the record is what it is: POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as trip_record.actual_distance_km 5.2 minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 4.6, which is 0.60 km, and it sets a tolerance of 1.0 km, so on the platform's recorded distances the deviation is within tolerance and the rider does not dispute those figures. The rider's case is therefore not that the detour was long but that it was neither justified under POL-RD-23 nor notified under POL-RD-21, and the rider asks the judge to record both findings; the rider does not ask the judge to depart from the tolerance or from POL-RD-24.

The rider's contested sum is pegged to the policy rather than to the headline figure. The fare the deviation accounts for is the excess distance fare POL-RD-24 defines - deviation distance 0.60 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, without surge - which is 0.43 SGD, and the 2.00 SGD in the claim is not a figure the policy measures. If a refund issues on this record it is 0.43 SGD, not 2.00; the rider asks for no more than the policy provides and does not ask the judge for a remedy outside POL-RD-24.

The driver's remaining assertion - that the 'Siglap side also about the same distance' - is contradicted by the record's own distances: 5.2 km actual against 4.6 km recommended is a 0.60 km excess on POL-RD-22's measure, so on the platform's own figures the Siglap route was longer than the recommended Bedok Road route, and the driver's minimisation of the detour is not supported by the record.

The deviation on this trip is 0.60 km, not the wide detour the rider's claim implies. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation as the platform's recorded actual distance minus the recommended distance: trip_record.actual_distance_km is 5.2 km and trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 4.6 km, so 5.2 - 4.6 = 0.60 km. The sparse GPS trace is not used to re-measure that distance, and need not be.
POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km. A deviation of 0.60 km is inside that tolerance, so this reroute is within tolerance as a matter of the policy's own arithmetic and cannot found a refund.

The traffic advisory covering the recommended route segment in the trip window is type NONE — it records no closure, no congestion and no incident — so under POL-RD-23 the reroute is not traffic-justified. With a 0.60 km deviation that puts the case squarely in POL-RD-24 row (e): not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less, no refund, within tolerance.

The answer is the same on the other branch of the matrix, so there is no open road to a refund here: POL-RD-24 row (c) — traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation 1 km or less — also returns no refund, within tolerance. Whichever way the traffic question falls, a 0.60 km deviation yields NO_ACTION. The driver's own counter-statement that 'Bedok Road got bus stop and traffic light very long' is a bare assertion which, under POL-RD-23, does not by itself justify a reroute; but that costs the driver nothing, because the tolerance row decides the case either way.

I concede the notice point on the record as it stands: the chat log holds two messages only, the last sent at 11:26:52, and the deviation was detected at 11:30:14, so the POL-RD-21 duty to tell the rider of the deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation is not made out, and in_app_calls is empty so no call recording can establish a verbal notice either. That omission still moves no money, because on a deviation of 1 km or less POL-RD-24 makes no refund conditional on notice — rows (c) and (e) both return NO_ACTION.

The rider's figure of $2.00 is not the measure of anything in this policy. POL-RD-24's excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd — 0.60 x 0.72 = 0.43 SGD — so even on a refund row the most this trip could return is 0.43 SGD, nowhere near the whole 2.00 SGD the rider asks back. The claim as filed cannot be sustained on the policy's own formula.

The present payment state is that the metered fare was charged and no refund has been issued: the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filer's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the rider pays the fare, the driver keeps it, and no money moves. That is the outcome the driver asks for.

This is the AI's ruling to make, not a human's. The contested value is 2.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence; POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied and is not met in any event at 0.60 km. Every artifact POL-RD-24 requires — trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown, chat log and traffic advisory — is present and admissibility-COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no fact the applied row needs is missing or impaired and POL-GEN-26's escalation does not arise.

Nothing on the driver's profile can decide, or assist in deciding, this trip: POL-GEN-01 makes every field on it except fraud_flags context only, and driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0, so the fraud-flag uplift in POL-GEN-22 is not triggered. Any argument built on the driver's prior flags is barred by POL-GEN-01 and does not bear on whether this 0.60 km deviation is within tolerance.

ruling.explanation:
Both of your accounts, and the platform's own record, agree on what matters here. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the platform's recorded distances: trip_record.actual_distance_km 5.2 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 4.6 km = 0.60 km, and it sets the tolerance at 1.0 km. A 0.60 km deviation is within tolerance, and neither party asks the judge to depart from those figures. POL-RD-24 row (e) therefore governs: the reroute was not traffic-justified — the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05002-01) is type NONE, and although it covers Bedok Road (the recommended road) and the trip window, it records no closure, congestion or incident, so POL-RD-23 is not satisfied and the driver's assertion of slow traffic does not stand in for that data — and a non-justified deviation of 1 km or less returns no refund. The traffic-justified branch reaches the same result: row (c) also returns no refund on a deviation of 1 km or less, so no refund is payable whether or not the reroute was justified. On the driver's duty to notify under POL-RD-21, the chat log (EV-CHAT-05002) holds two messages, both sent at 11:26 and both about the pickup point, the deviation was detected at 11:30:14, in_app_calls is empty, and no call recording establishes a verbal notice — so an agreed deviation is not made out; but within tolerance no refund turns on notice. The rider's figure of $2.00 is not one POL-RD-24 measures: the excess distance fare would be 0.60 × per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 = 0.43 SGD, and it does not arise at all because the deviation is within tolerance. The rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the metered fare of 9.42 SGD was charged and no refund issued (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The driver's profile plays no part: POL-GEN-01 makes its fields context only and driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0. The contested value is 2.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so this ruling is final at any confidence, and every artifact POL-RD-24 reads is present and COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26's escalation does not arise.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
